31 Two metal plates are a distance of 30 cm apart in a vacuum.
A current exists between the two plates consisting of electrons moving at a constant speed of
1.5 × 106
m s–1.
At any instant, there is always just one electron travelling between the plates.
What is the current between the plates?
A
3.2 × 10–26
A
B
8.0 × 10–13
A
C
1.6 × 10–12
A
D
2.0 × 10–7
A

hints: Notice the wording 'just one electron travelling between the plates' - the charge delivered in one crossing is one elementary charge $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.
Recall $I = Q/t$, so you need the time $t$ for that one electron to cross the $30 \text{ cm}$ gap at $1.5 \times 10^{6} \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Convert $30 \text{ cm}$ to $0.30 \text{ m}$, calculate $t = d/v$, then divide $1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ by that $t$ to get $I$ in $\text{A}$.
walkthrough: Identify the charge per crossing: because there is always just one electron in flight, $Q = e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ passes from one plate region to the other per transit.
Find the transit time from constant speed: $t = d/v$ with $d = 30 \text{ cm} = 0.30 \text{ m}$ and $v = 1.5 \times 10^{6} \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Substitute: $t = 0.30 / (1.5 \times 10^{6}) = 2.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ s}$. This is the time for one elementary charge to be transferred.
Use the definition of current: $I = Q/t = e/t$.
Substitute values with units: $I = (1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}) / (2.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ s}) = 8.0 \times 10^{-13} \text{ A}$.

A.explanation: This multiplies charge by time, $e \times t$, giving $3.2 \times 10^{-26}$. Current is charge divided by time, not multiplied.

B.explanation: The transit time is $2.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ s}$ and $I = e/t$ gives $8.0 \times 10^{-13} \text{ A}$.

C.explanation: This is twice the correct current, from using half the correct transit time for the $30 \text{ cm}$ gap at $1.5 \times 10^{6} \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: This is the electron transit time $t = 2.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ s}$, not a current in $\text{A}$.
